name: Pessac-Léognan

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
One of the two regional appellations allowed anywhere in Bordeaux, beside plain Bordeaux. Together they cover about half the Bordeaux vineyard.

In 1855 brokers ranked Bordeaux estates by reputation and price. Reds were ranked from first to fifth growths, nearly all in the Médoc, and the sweet whites of Sauternes and Barsac from superior first growth to second growth.
A ranking for Médoc châteaux left out of the 1855 classification. Any Médoc property may apply.
Graves classified its red wines in 1953 and added dry whites in 1959. All the classified estates sit in Pessac-Léognan.
keyfacts: The appellation was created in 1987, and before then the area was part of the Graves AOC.
It lies in the northern part of Graves, on the left bank of the Garonne, bordering the city of Bordeaux to the west and south.
It includes Château Haut-Brion, the only red-wine producer outside the Haut-Médoc classified in the 1855 classification, and all the châteaux in the 1959 Graves classification.
Red wines are led by Cabernet Sauvignon, often with Merlot and Cabernet Franc, while dry whites are mainly Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon.
The soils are mainly gravel and sandy gravel left by the ancient Garonne, in places three meters deep or more.

notes: Pessac-Léognan is equally famous for reds and dry whites, though red still leads.
Reds typically taste of blackcurrant and cedar and are often called earthy.
The whites taste of nectarine when young and of nuts, honey and custard after 7 to 15 years.
Its oak-aged Sauvignon Blanc blends are among the few Sauvignons that age well.

blurb.text: The northern part of Graves in Bordeaux, making red and dry white wines, with red over 80% of the wine. It includes Château Haut-Brion, and its classed growths are about a third of its estates.
